verdict.rationale: Godot's full engine source is public on GitHub under the MIT license, with official compilation instructions for every supported platform. The license explicitly permits distributing changed versions. Community reports of contributing PRs and critiquing the engine's internal pathfinding code confirm developers read and modify the source in practice. Missing for 10: the compilation guide itself is only referenced, not excerpted, so the custom-build workflow depth is unevidenced in the pack.

support.subject: As a game developer, I can read and modify the full engine source when I hit a wall

citations.quote: Godot is completely free and open source under the very permissive MIT license. No strings attached, no royalties, nothing.
See the official docs for compilation instructions for every supported platform.
You can distribute unmodified and changed versions of Godot Engine, even commercially and under a different license (including proprietary)
Once you start contributing to Godot, it's pretty addicting.
